title: Predict: Range Operators
hints: `...` includes the upper bound; `..<` stops before it.
jsBridge: JS has no range operators. Swift has `...` (closed), `..<` (half-open) and one-sided `2...`/`..<5`. They're values you can store and pass around, and slicing uses them directly.

compass.q: `Range` vs `ClosedRange` vs `PartialRangeFrom`: which can you iterate over, and which can't you?
What's the JS idiom for `0..<n` (`Array.from({length: n}, (_, i) => i)`)? What does it allocate?
Can you iterate `1.0...2.0`? Why not? What do you use instead?
`array[..<3]` is a common way to take the first 3. What does `prefix(3)` do differently for short arrays?
